title: A polynomial ring in finitely many variables over a field is a regular ring
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $n\ge0$ an integer and $P=k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ the polynomial ring [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Then $P$ is a regular ring [def-weil-regular-scheme]: $P$ is Noetherian, and for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset P$ the localization $P_{\mathfrak p}$ is a regular local ring, i.e. a Noetherian local ring whose maximal ideal $\mathfrak pP_{\mathfrak p}$ can be generated by $\dim P_{\mathfrak p}$ elements ($\dim$ the Krull dimension).
